description: The CPDS-AD research team publishes detection baselines for its cyber-physical distribution-network testbed through GitHub and a versioned Zenodo software archive. The package includes Transformer, LSTM and temporal-convolution reconstruction models, pretrained checkpoints and evaluation scripts for false-data anomalies. Separate communication-anomaly baselines use statistical scores, isolation forests and nearest neighbours. The documented environment uses Python 3.11 and PyTorch, including CPU execution. Inputs follow the CPDS-AD five-second measurements and traffic windows from a 13-node laboratory system; outputs are anomaly scores and detection measures, not electrical power-flow results. Zenodo version 2.0.1, released on 27 September 2026, states CC BY 4.0 and provides free access. GitHub does not identify a licence in its API metadata, so the archive is the stated licence source. Some baselines fit transductively to the evaluation distribution, which matters when interpreting reported detection performance. These models can represent detection behaviour in resilience experiments alongside platform-opendss. Code execution and transfer to operational networks were not tested here.
